I was browsing through the subverses (filtered by most popular) to see which ones appealed to me. A lot of the same ones I loved from Reddit are on here, and that's great! Some new ones too, which I find interesting.

But here comes my perspective which may be a bit... unfavorable? I'm willing to discuss it. I may simply be looking at this wrong. But when filtering the subverses by popularity... things like jailbait, cringe, fatpeoplehate, and SJWhate come up toward the top. Now before you assume anything, just know: we all agree that this site is about having communities which will not be censored. I am not trying to dismiss that, and I believe these communities have a right to exist. What I want to know is... does this reflect the majority of the userbase here? Is this community filled with people stuck in their hate for others?

I'll be upfront about this. I am a 25-year-old female who has been playing video games since she was a toddler. I simply want to enjoy what is by far my most relatable community--gaming (and DBZ). I do not want to be harassed here like I am when I play games online (which is manageable, and sometimes funny). I do not want to be dismissed when I speak of my personal anecdotes involving sexism in the gaming community. I do not want to be quizzed for my "validity" as a gamer. But most of all, I do not want to be pigeon-holed into labels like "SJW" and "feminazi" when I simply disagree.

I am actually quite a moderate person who usually doesn't give a shit. Tifa should keep her tits in the upcoming remake. Games with scantily clad women should totally exist. I think the industry is actually pretty fair and balanced nowadays, and I like that women are being represented more equally. I don't really have any complaints, honestly. But when I do feel like I'm being harassed or oppressed in some way... I want to know that this is a welcoming community. And if it isn't... I'll move on, simple as that.

I do not typically voice my opinion like this. I'm afraid of being labeled as some fat, ugly, Tumblr, triggered bitch... when reality is quite the opposite. I'm just hoping Voat will be more moderate and have room for nuanced discussion when these topics DO come up.

I usually avoid anonymous social justice discussions altogether--from both sides. And I'm often in the grey area that no one agrees with anyway. But it would nice to be involved in a community that can actually talk about social issues civilly. And I know there are a lot of women out there just like me, who feel silenced in their moderate opinions. Women looking for a place to be a gamer and not have to defend our gender as a whole whenever gamergate comes up. ("But not all women are feminazis!" --something I hope is completely obvious and never has to be said.)

I guess I'll know how understanding this community is based on the responses I get. Thanks for taking your time to read my perspective!
